Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
1205 PM PDT Sat Sep 12 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
A cooling and drying trend will occur across the region into the 
weekend and early next week. This will be accompanied by a building 
marine layer with clouds returning closer to the coastal areas each 
night and morning. An area of high pressure may strengthen by the 
end of next week, nudging temperatures back above average.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO 
COUNTIES...

High pressure continues to weaken over the region today with 
stronger onshore flow seen at current observations. This has allowed 
for a deepening marine layer, where some places along the coast saw 
low clouds and patchy fog earlier this morning. Looking toward the 
lunch hour, temperatures a relatively cooler with highs in the 70s 
to near 90 west of the mountains. Elevated westerly winds will also 
be felt across the mountains and deserts with wind gusts 20-40 MPH. 

An area of low pressure off the west coast of British Columbia will 
continue to push southward today, eventually moving into the Pacific 
Northwest this weekend. This weather pattern will help bring in more 
cooler air and greater extent to the marine layer into far western 
valleys. We can expect to cool a few degrees each day with breezy 
westerly winds across the mountains and deserts each afternoon and 
evening. Temperatures will be near average by the weekend, with 
highs dipping below average by next Monday and Tuesday.  High 
temperatures may stay below 90 degrees for areas west of the 
mountains with highs closer to 100 degrees over the Coachella 
Valley. Low temperatures will also begin to cool off through early 
next week as well with lows in the 50s and 60s along and west of the 
mountains and up in the high desert.

High pressure over the Southern Plains may expand further into the 
desert southwest by the end of next week. The placement and strength 
of this system is still uncertain, but many models are hinting that 
another subtle warm up may take place by this time. NBM shows highs 
approaching 100 across inland valleys with 70s and 80s closer to the 
coast and across the mountains.

&&

.AVIATION... 
121730Z...Coasts...VFR through the late afternoon, though some low 
clouds near 1500 ft MSL may stick to the beaches. High confidence on 
low clouds returning to coastal TAF sites and up to 15 miles inland 
after 01Z Sun with bases 1200-1700 ft MSL. Low confidence on cigs 
making into the Inland Empire and VCTY KONT after 10z. Vis 
reductions most likely on higher coastal terrain. Scatter out Sunday 
similar to this morning near 16-18Z. 

S/W winds gusting over 30 kts at times 20z Sat-06z across mountain 
passes into the deserts. Otherwise, FEW clouds above 15 kft and VFR 
conditions through Sunday.

&&

.MARINE...
West-northwest winds expected to gust up to 20 knots in the 
afternoons through Sunday over outer coastal waters. Otherwise, no 
hazardous marine conditions are expected through Wednesday.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.
